acip: MA GRUB NA, SPYI CHOS CAN, SHES BYA'I SPYI DANG BYE BRAG GANG RUNG GI BYE BRAG YIN PAR THAL, KHYOD SHES BYA'I SPYI DANG BYE BRAG GANG RUNG YIN, KHYOD SHES BYA'I SPYI DANG BYE BRAG GANG RUNG DANG BDAG GCIG TU 'BREL, KHYOD MA YIN ZHING SHES BYA'I SPYI DANG BYE BRAG GANG RUNG YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA DU MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: ma grub na, spyi chos can, shes bya'i spyi dang bye brag gang rung gi bye brag yin par thal, khyod shes bya'i spyi dang bye brag gang rung yin, khyod shes bya'i spyi dang bye brag gang rung dang bdag gcig tu 'brel, khyod ma yin zhing shes bya'i spyi dang bye brag gang rung yin pa'i gzhi mthun pa du ma grub pa'i phyir
english: I disagree that qualities are characteristic of either a quality of knowable things, or of something which is characteristic of knowable things. Suppose you do disagree. In that case, let's consider, one more time, qualities. They are so characteristic of either a quality of knowable things, or of something which is characteristic of knowable things, Because (1) they are either a quality of knowable things, or characteristic of knowable things; (2) they are related to that which is either a quality of knowable things, or characteristic of knowable things, in such a way that to be them is to be it; and (3) there exist many examples of things which are not them, but which are still either a quality of knowable things, or of something which is characteristic of knowable things.
